quizzes.title: Type Basics Checkpoint
quizzes.description: Covers: Introduction & Setup, Basic Types, Typing Functions.

questions.prompt: Which command installs TypeScript as a development tool in a project?
questions.explanation: npm install -D adds a package to devDependencies. It gives you the tsc compiler for the project.
nums has 3 items, and pair[0] is the first tuple item, "Ali".

questions.prompt: What type does TypeScript infer for let count = 5;?
questions.explanation: TypeScript looks at the starting value 5 and infers number. You do not need to write the type.

questions.prompt: Why is unknown safer than any?
options: You must check the type before using the value
questions.explanation: With unknown the compiler makes you narrow the type first. With any the compiler stops checking.
The second parameter is omitted, so the default value "Hello" is used.
Adding two numbers gives a number, so the return type is number.

quizzes.title: Object Types Checkpoint
quizzes.description: Covers: Interfaces & Type Aliases, Union Types & Narrowing, Classes & Access Modifiers.

questions.prompt: Which of these can only be written with a type alias, not an interface?
options: A union such as string | number
An object with an optional property
An object with a readonly property
questions.explanation: Interfaces describe object shapes. A union of types needs a type alias.
The kind is "square", so the code returns side * side, which is 4 * 4 = 16.

questions.prompt: Where can a private class member be used?
options: Inside the class and its subclasses
questions.explanation: private limits access to the class itself. protected also allows subclasses.
Parameter properties declare and set owner and balance automatically. show() is inside the class, so it may read the private balance.

questions.prompt: Which check narrows a value of type string | number to string?
questions.explanation: The typeof check is the usual way to narrow primitive types.
A question mark after the property name makes it optional.

questions.prompt: In function first<T>(arr: T[]): T, what is T when you call first(["a", "b"])?
questions.explanation: T is inferred from the argument. An array of strings makes T equal to string.
Index 1 of [10, 20, 30] is 20, and index 0 of ["a", "b"] is "a".
Partial makes all properties optional. It is useful for update objects.
A Record<string, number> accepts any string key, so adding sci makes three keys.

options: A new type that has every User property except password
questions.explanation: Omit builds a new type by leaving out the listed keys.

questions.prompt: Fill in the utility type that makes all properties optional.
questions.explanation: Partial<User> makes name and age optional, so an object with only name is allowed.
